title: Air-spaced triplet telescope objective, f/2.8 (optiland sample)

collection.attribution: optiland (MIT, Copyright (c) 2024 Kramer Harrison), TripletTelescopeObjective: three air-spaced N-BK7 / N-BK7 / SF1 elements at f/2.8. The design reference printed in the sample is kept; the cited book or patent is not redistributed.
collection.redistribution: optiland is MIT-licensed and publishes these surface data. The transcription, the native Project and this evidence extract are MIT. The design reference named in the sample is attributed, not redistributed.

aperture_validity.basis: The source marks surface 1 as the stop. A stop on a refracting surface is that surface's clear aperture: the Project carries no opaque plate, so light outside the clear aperture misses the lens rather than being stopped by a plate.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: There is no stop plate to evaluate a pupil or illumination quantity against, so no stop-dependent match is claimed.
aperture_validity.consequence: The record supports first-order and structural queries; a stop-dependent constraint stays unconfirmed.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: The sample enables three wavelengths in air (0.4861, 0.5876 and 0.6563 um, d and F and C); each is converted once to the vacuum wavelength the engine evaluates. The committed Project traces the primary 587.6 nm sample; the other two are recorded because the sample enables them and the triplet is corrected over that band.
spectrum.wavelength_precision: Full precision samples; no rounding in the Project.

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The source enables 3 samples and states no continuous range.

spectrum.engine_evaluation_note: The committed Project traces the primary sample; the other samples are recorded because the source enables them.

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: Thick-lens ABCD through the committed Project at the reference wavelength.

comparison.rule: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * |source|. atol covers the printed precision of the stated focal length; rtol covers the printed precision of the radii and thicknesses, the constant-index material model and the engine's air-referenced index convention.

effective_focal_length.basis: The source prints no focal length for this example, so no source value exists.

back_focal_length.source_basis: The sample's last surface spacing: its own paraxial solve places the image plane at the rear focus, so that spacing is the back focal distance from the final vertex.

f_number.convention: Image-space f-number as printed for the example.
f_number.definition: image-space f-number; this is the system aperture the record declares, taken from the value the source states for the example

entrance_pupil_diameter_mm.definition: Diameter of the modelled aperture that bounds the axial beam

entrance_pupil_f_number.definition: Magnitude of effective focal length divided by the admitted axial entrance pupil diameter.

field.definition: Field angle; the full field is twice the stated half field
field.note: The sample states an image-space f-number of 2.8 and no focal length.
field.field_points_basis: The field points the source enables, in degrees, half-angle.

materials.basis: Every element is a constant index equal to its printed nd, valid at the reference wavelength only; the printed vd values are kept in the evidence extract.

approximations.statement: Each element is a constant index equal to its printed nd, valid only at the reference wavelength; the printed vd values are kept in the evidence extract but are not modelled.

The sample states no clear semi-diameters. Each element is given one clear diameter: the largest of the paraxial marginal-ray and chief-ray envelopes over its own surfaces (marginal ray through the stated entrance pupil, chief ray at the field points the sample enables), times a 2 per cent mechanical margin. The envelope is a minimum clear aperture, so every surface of the element passes the axial beam and the chief ray at the full stated field. It is a buildable estimate, not a drawing: no vignetting beyond the stop is modelled and no vignetting figure is claimed.

notes: The sample prints no focal length, so the paraxial state stays NOT_CHECKED even though the sample's own solved back focus is compared and agrees.

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline
